deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics. It is the end of a section of German notes on ancient Greek history, apparently lecture or textbook notes in the style of a Heeren-type 'Geschichte der Staaten des Alterthums'. The next page opens 'Vierter Abschnitt. Geschichte der Macedonischen Monarchie'. The page finishes the account of the Third Sacred War and Philip II's entry into Greek affairs.

Content, translated:
- Philip had himself enrolled among the Amphictyons. This picks up the previous page's '...unter welche sich Philipp einschreiben' with '...ließ.'
- Having taken the first step, he soon took the second.
- In 339 he came into Greece a second time with an army, because the Locrians (of Amphissa) had again profaned a piece of sacred land.
- He had the expedition entrusted to him and seized the fortified town of Elatea.
- All the Greeks rose to drive him out of Greece, but in 338 he defeated the united army (at Chaeronea) and placed garrisons in their cities.

A horizontal rule closes the section. There is no derivation to reconstruct. The hand and subject suggest copied history notes bound into the Nachlass bundle, not Gauss's own mathematical work.
errors: No mathematical errors, since there is no mathematics. The historical content (Fourth Sacred War against Amphissa in 339, seizure of Elatea, Chaeronea in 338) is standard and correct.
On the previous page, Philomelus's death is given as 353; modern chronology usually places the battle of Neon in 354 BC. This is a minor point and outside this page.
